newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares surge on hopes of markets steps.
newsitem.headline: India shares surge on hopes of markets steps.

text.p: Indian stocks surged over three percent on Monday on growing expectation of a government package that would stimulate the capital markets and woo investment, dealers said.
The markets have been buoyant since the New Year in sharp contrast with the bearish mood afflicting other Asian markets and broad losses registered on Friday on Wall Street.
"People are building up positions in front-bench stocks...nobody wants to miss the rally," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
At 3.05 p.m. (0935 GMT), the benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange was up 105.62 points, or 3.07 percent, at 3,541.24 in hectic trade.
The Delhi Stock Exchange Sensitive Index was up 30.62 points or 4.22 percent at 756.40 at 1.00 p.m. (0730 GMT).
The Bombay stock index has risen around 15 percent this year inspired by a pledge by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on December 31 to unveil market-boosting policy initiatives.
Gowda has since held confidence-boosting talks with stock exchange chiefs, industry captains and bankers on the subject.
"There's always hope and anticipation..nobody wants to get caught on the wrong side of the market..," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at James Capel B&K.
Traders said hesitation on the part of investors and local funds to sell stocks in a rising market coupled with increased speculative buy orders was stoking the price rally.
"People are not very lenient on the selling side...lack of liquidity of stocks is one of the major reasons spurring the market to higher levels," said Capel's Sanghvi.
The policy measures due by mid-January are now expected to be presented before the Indian premier leaves on January 31 for a World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
Some of the possible steps include allowing companies to buy back their shares to reduce an equity overhang in the market, and scrapping taxes on shareholders' dividends, analysts said.
The enthusiasm persisted despite a government dampener.

A government spokesman on Monday said Gowda, who was scheduled to address The All India Association of Industries at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) in Bombay was not expected to announce any capital market measures.
"The visit to Bombay is not connected to the capital markets. It has nothing to do with the capital markets," he told Reuters.
Asked if a package of measures was due to be announced this week, the spokesman said: "There are always a few things on the drawing board."
Dealers had said the government might also raise the ceiling on foreign institutional holdings in State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, to 24 from 20 percent.
A Finance Ministry official reiterated that the government was not expected to announce a single package of measures before Deve Gowda and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave for Davos.
"People are realising better value..the little bit of profit-taking is nullified by fresh speculative bidding," Capel's Sanghvi said. "There is all-round buying interest in the market."
